en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
Naggavagga 24.
The Training Rule on Wearing the Outer Robe:
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs, having placed their robes in the hands of other bhikkhunīs, set out on a journey through the countryside wearing only their inner and upper garments.
Those robes, having been left for a long time, became moth-eaten.
The bhikkhunīs then had to dry them in the sun.
Those bhikkhunīs said this to those bhikkhunīs:
“Venerable ladies, whose robes are these with frayed edges?
Then those bhikkhunīs reported this matter to the bhikkhunīs.
Those bhikkhunīs who were modest … [as before] … complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:

“How can these bhikkhunīs, having placed their robes in the hands of other bhikkhunīs, set out on a journey through the country wearing only their inner and upper robes? … [The Buddha asked: “Is it true, monks, that bhikkhunīs do this?”
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:

“… How indeed, monks, can these bhikkhunīs, having placed their robes in the hands of other bhikkhunīs, set out on a journey through the country wearing only their inner and upper robes? This is not suitable…” [as before].
“Monks, this does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And thus, monks, should the nuns recite this training rule:
‘If any bhikkhunī should let the five-day period for the distribution of the outer robe (saṅghāṭi) pass by, it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).’”
"But whichever" means whichever such... "nun" means...
[as before]... nun.
... [as before] ... this is the nun intended in this context.
"Should she let the five-day period for the distribution of the outer robe (saṅghāṭi) pass" means:
if on the fifth day she neither wears, nor puts on, nor dries the five robes, and thus lets the fifth day pass, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If five days have elapsed and she perceives that they have elapsed, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If five days have elapsed and she is unsure of it, there is an offense of expiation.
If five days have elapsed and she perceives that they have not elapsed, there is an offense of expiation.
If five days have not elapsed, but she perceives that they have elapsed, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If five days have not elapsed, but she is in doubt, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If five days have not elapsed, and she perceives that they have not elapsed, there is no offense.
There is no offense if,
on the fifth day, she wears, puts on, or dries five robes;
or if she is ill.
In cases of misfortune,
for one who is insane,
and for one who is a first-time offender.
The fourth training rule is concluded.
